content.text:
The analysis shows that Zone_F3_Z01 (Core_mid)'s temperature follows the same seasonal pattern as every other zone in the building. It rises in summer (months 7-11) because of the outdoor climate and falls in winter (months 12-2) just like all other zones. There is no anomalous deviation from the other zones from July 2018 onward — all zones track together.

Critically:
- The data shows NO divergence between Zone_F3_Z01 and the peer zones after July 2018.
- The "local load change" hypothesis would predict a sustained offset from peer zones driven by increased heat gain — not present.
- The "zone sensor fault" hypothesis would predict a frozen or clearly offset reading (like the F2_Z06..F2_Z09 zones pinned at 27.0, classic sensor faults) — also not present for F3_Z01; F3_Z01 still varies naturally and tracks peers.
- The premise that the temperature has "risen relative to other zones since July 2018" is not supported by the data.

Since the data does not support either candidate cause, the streams available cannot tell these causes apart — but I should abstain because neither cause is supported by the data.
